newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares hit new high for fourth straight day.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares hit new high for fourth straight day.

text.p: Danish share prices closed at a new all-time high on Thursday, despite some profit-taking, having set new records every day this week so far.
Dealers said there were good chances of further gains on Friday, but much would depend on U.S. employment figures due out at 1230 GMT on Friday.
The KFX top-20 index gained 0.14 point to 124.60 on Thursday, in overall bourse turnover of 869 million crowns.
"Technically we're talking about a need to consolidate around 125, with 127-30 in view as the next stop, but tomorrow's (U.S.) data could upset things," a dealer said.
Denmark releases its own trade and current account figures for July at 0730 GMT on Friday, but they are seen as having less market impact than the U.S. numbers.
Analysts say that the rising Copenhagen market should be seen in the light of a generally buoyant economy, low interest rates and a good deal of foreign buying interest.
The KFX December future rose 0.85 point to 125.10 with 10 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Thursday's index rise was the result of individual gains of around one to two percent across a wide range of shares, with no individual paper standing out.
Bigest loser was FLS Industries, plunging 22.3 crowns to 760 crowns after profit-taking, a dealer said.
